title: The Day the Page Woke Up
skyStory: Welcome, you two. The moon is brand new tonight, only two percent lit, curled up in Sagittarius like a cat pretending to be asleep. It has been waiting for this page to open since October and is trying very hard to look casual. Mars brought streamers. Saturn brought a clipboard. A November gale rattles the shutters, which is the sky's version of a drumroll.

reading: First day of a brand-new reading, and the Tiger has already opened four tabs about it. Lovely. Close three. A new moon is a seed, not a forest, and the [[Knight of Wands]] would like you to plant exactly one thing today and then walk away whistling.

Around 11:40 am somebody will thank you for something you forgot you did. Do not wave it off. Do not say it was nothing. Say thank you back, out loud, with your whole face, and let it land like snow on a mitten. Life Path 3 means words are your fire. Today, practise catching them as well as throwing them. Ten points to the Tiger for every compliment received without a rebuttal.
joel.mission: Write one sentence about what you hope this month brings, fold it into a tiny square, and tuck it somewhere you will forget.
joel.omen: A chimney puffing smoke in a perfectly straight line. The cabin approves of new beginnings and says keep going.
joel.stoneWhy: Nancy's stone, for a first page

reading: Hello, Mountain. The sky has been rehearsing its welcome speech for you all week and still fumbled the opening line. It is fine. You have told enough stories to know the good part always comes in the middle, after the hands start moving.

A new moon in Sagittarius wants to know where you are headed, and you are allowed to answer: somewhere with a good view and a warm drink. The Wood Rat in you has already noticed something small that nobody else has, maybe a crooked picture frame or a word misspelled on a sign. Keep it to yourself until 4 pm, then tell it as the best story of the day.
nancy.mission: Turn the ruby on your pinky to face outward for one whole conversation, like a tiny lighthouse beam.
nancy.omen: A gull standing on one leg on something it definitely should not be standing on. Bold choices are in season.
nancy.stoneWhy: the Fire is watching over you

together.text: Send each other one word that sums up how this month should feel, without conferring. Compare them at bedtime. If they match, the cabin chimney puffs twice. If they do not, combine them into one ridiculous new word and use it all week.
